{{Short description|Episodes of Japanese anime series}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:List of ''Bleach'' episodes}}
[[File:Bleachanime.png|thumb|Key visual for the original series]]

''[[Bleach (TV series)|Bleach]]'' is a Japanese [[anime]] television series based on [[Tite Kubo]]'s [[manga]] ''[[Bleach (manga)|Bleach]]''. It was directed by [[Noriyuki Abe]], produced by [[TV Tokyo]], [[Dentsu]] and [[Studio Pierrot]], and aired in Japan from October 5, 2004, to March 27, 2012, running for a total of 366 episodes.<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|title=Bleach TV Anime Ending on March 27|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2012-02-23/bleach-tv-anime-ending-on-march-27|publisher=animenewsnetwork.com|access-date=18 September 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120915060917/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2012-02-23/bleach-tv-anime-ending-on-march-27|archive-date=15 September 2012}}</ref> The series follows the adventures of high school student [[Ichigo Kurosaki]] who can see spirits and becomes a [[List of Soul Reapers in Bleach|Soul Reaper]], after assuming the duties of Soul Reaper [[Rukia Kuchiki]].

[[Viz Media]] obtained the foreign television, home video and merchandising rights to the ''Bleach'' anime from TV Tokyo Corporation and [[Shueisha]] on March 15, 2006.<ref>{{Cite press release|url=http://www.viz.com/news/newsroom/2006/03_bleach.php|title=Viz Media named master licensor for hit Japanese action manga Shōnen Jump's Bleach|publisher=Viz Media|access-date=2007-04-01|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070504033042/http://www.viz.com/news/newsroom/2006/03_bleach.php|archive-date=2007-05-04}}</ref> Subsequently, Viz Media contracted [[Studiopolis]] to create the English adaptation of the anime, and has licensed its individual ''Bleach'' merchandising rights to several different companies.<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2006-11-02/viz-announces-bleach-merchandise-licenses|title=Viz Announces Bleach Merchandise Licenses|publisher=Anime News Network|access-date=2007-03-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070326181450/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2006-11-02/viz-announces-bleach-merchandise-licenses|archive-date=2007-03-26}}</ref> The English adaptation of the ''Bleach'' anime premiered on Canada's [[YTV (Canadian TV channel)|YTV]] in their [[Bionix (TV programming block)|Bionix]] programming block on September 9, 2006. [[Cartoon Network]] in the U.S. began airing ''Bleach'' the following evening on September 10 as part of [[Adult Swim]].

Forty-five pieces of [[theme music]] are used for the episodes: Fifteen opening themes and thirty closing themes. Several CDs that contain the theme music and other tracks have been released by Studio Pierrot.<ref name="StudioPierrotCDs">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://pierrot.jp/title/bleach/goods/cd/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080227031229/http://pierrot.jp/title/bleach/goods/cd/|archive-date=2008-02-27|title=Bleach Goods Search – CDs|language=ja|publisher=[[Studio Pierrot]]|access-date=2008-01-17}}</ref>

A follow-up sequel series that adapts the final story arc from the manga, titled ''[[Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War]]'', aired from October 11, 2022, to October 27, 2026. It was directed by [[Tomohisa Taguchi]]{{efn|{{Nihongo|Director|監督}} for Parts 1–2 and {{Nihongo|Chief Director|総監督}} for Parts 3–4}} and Hikaru Murata{{efn|{{Nihongo|Chief Episode Director|チーフ演出}} for Parts 1–2 and {{Nihongo|Director|監督}} for Parts 3–4}} and produced by the same companies as the original series but with the addition of the manga's publishing company, [[Shueisha]].

{{#invoke:Episode list|list
| EpisodeNumber = 1
| Title         = ''Bleach'' Jump Festa 2004 Anime Tour: Memories in the Rain
| ShortSummary  = This special, shown in Japan at the [[Jump Festa]] 2004 Anime Tour, is a [[television pilot|pilot episode]] for the series. It focuses more on [[Ichigo Kurosaki|Ichigo]]'s feelings regarding his mother's death. [[Tite Kubo]], the creator of ''Bleach'', voices [[List of Bleach characters#Kon|Kon]] in this special instead of [[Mitsuaki Madono]], the original voice actor of Kon. The closing theme used for the episode is "Memories in the Rain" by [[Masakazu Morita]], the voice actor of Ichigo, and [[Fumiko Orikasa]], the voice actress of [[Rukia Kuchiki|Rukia]]. This special serves as an alternative version of episodes 8 and 9 of the anime series.
| LineColor     = FCA845
}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|list
| EpisodeNumber = 2
| Title         = ''Bleach'' Jump Festa 2005 Anime Tour: The Sealed Sword Frenzy
| ShortSummary  = This special, shown in Japan at the Jump Festa 2005 Anime Tour, is set after the events of [[List of Bleach episodes (season 3)|season three]] (after episode 63). Baishin, a [[List of Soul Reapers in Bleach|Soul Reaper]] sealed by [[Bleach (manga)#Setting|Soul Society]] four hundred years before the start of the series, escapes his confinement. He battles Ichigo and drains half of his spiritual energy. To aid Ichigo, Rukia, [[Renji Abarai|Renji]] and several other Soul Reaper captains travel to the world of the living. After using his [[List of Soul Reapers in Bleach#Characteristics|bankai]], Baishin is able to fend off the various Soul Reapers, and is defeated by Ichigo Kurosaki after Ichigo uses his own bankai. Afterwards, Ichigo reveals that Baishin had fused with his ''[[List of Soul Reapers in Bleach|zanpakutō]]'' and was seeking a way to free himself from his sword. The closing theme for the episode is "Ditty For Daddy" by Shiro Sagisu.
| LineColor     = FCA845
}}
|}

=== English ===
The first 32 DVD compilations have been released by [[Viz Media]] in the United States.<ref name="VizDVD1"/><ref name="VizDVD32"/> 26 DVD collection box set of the series were released from June 10, 2008,<ref name="SeasonBox1"/> to September 29, 2015.<ref name="SeasonBox26"/> From July 19, 2016, to December 7, 2021, Viz released the series on Blu-Ray, with a total of 13 sets, half the number of DVD sets.

The series has been released in the United Kingdom by [[Manga Entertainment]] in half-season sets, then re-released into season sets.
